source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 transaction, constraint, concurrency, transaction-processing, WAL, durability-configuration, and deferred-constraint documentation plus SQLite atomic-commit documentation. All eight final official destinations returned HTTP 200. WAL and synchronous-commit claims are explicitly product/configuration scoped.

evidence: Checked transaction read/write sets R(T)/W(T), invariant I(S), log/page/durable frontiers, and commit/durability/acknowledgment/visibility timestamps.
Checked WAL ordering is conditional on an engine recovery protocol and is not generalized to journal, copy-on-write, or consensus implementations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Network clocks are not assumed synchronized and commit, durability, acknowledgment, and visibility remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed transfer from balances 100 and 50 by amount 30 as 70 and 80 with conserved total 150.
Recomputed duplicate request as no second change, overdraft 100 from balance 70 as rejection, and simulated pre-commit crash as unchanged 70/80 state.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The finite balances and single-threaded transitions are illustrative only.

evidence: Re-derived why operation effects and idempotency outcome must share one transaction.
Re-derived write-ahead ordering as durable recovery information preceding dependent safe page persistence.
Re-derived unknown outcome from commit-before-response and lookup/replay requirements.
Re-derived why page writeback is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of transaction commit.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The portable model separates guarantees from engine-specific mechanisms.

evidence: Reviewed invalid input, zero/negative amounts, missing entities, insufficient funds, duplicate identity, input mismatch, concurrent duplicates, and retention.
Reviewed lost update, write skew, blocking, deadlock, serialization rejection, deferred-constraint failure, trigger failure, and transaction-wide retry.
Reviewed timeout, cancellation, disconnect before/after commit, process/OS/power/device failure, torn writes, checkpoint overlap, recovery, network partition, replica lag, and correlated loss.
Reviewed log insertion/flush, page dirtiness/writeback, local/remote acknowledgment, downstream apply, external side effects, and outbox reconciliation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: A process-kill experiment is explicitly insufficient for power-loss or replicated-durability claims.

evidence: Validated nonnegative balances and conserved total before modeled commit.
Validated request-result uniqueness suppresses the modeled duplicate.
Validated rejected and discarded-workspace paths leave committed balances unchanged.
The verifier matched exact nine-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: Sequential Python assignments do not supply real atomicity, concurrency control, WAL, durability, or crash recovery.

evidence: Reviewed all finite transition branches and confirmed only validated workspace state replaces committed state.
Reviewed conservation and nonnegative predicates for the successful transfer.
Reviewed duplicate lookup before mutation and rejection before commit assignment.
Reviewed WAL frontier implication under its explicitly stated recovery assumption.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a database engine, filesystem, device, replication topology, or external system.

evidence: Separated statement success from transaction commit, log insertion from flush, dirty pages from persistence, local durability from replica stages, and commit from reader visibility.
Separated retryable rejection from unknown outcome and idempotent protocol from a correlation token.
Separated database atomicity from external side effects and process crash from OS/power/storage faults.
Separated portable transactional invariants from PostgreSQL WAL and SQLite journal mechanisms.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No ACID, synchronous, exactly-once, or durability label is used without qualifying semantics.

evidence: The standard-library finite transactional-state model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All eight final official reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live transaction, concurrent conflict, WAL flush, filesystem/device fault, crash recovery, replication, outbox, or external payment experiment was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently traces a write from business intent through validation, concurrency, physical effects, recovery logging, commit, durability, acknowledgment, visibility, cleanup, and outcome resolution.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed transaction scope, database constraints, conflict handling, retry taxonomy, idempotency, external effects, amplification, durability policy, replication boundaries, pooling, deadlines, crash testing, reconciliation, telemetry, and sensitive-data controls.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, finite ledger model, ten distinct cases, and five design/recovery exercises progress from basic write stages to production-grade uncertain-outcome and crash reasoning.

limitations: Internal authoring, official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify any live transaction, constraint, trigger, lock, isolation history, idempotency implementation, WAL/journal, log or page flush, filesystem/device contract, checkpoint, crash recovery, replication acknowledgment, external effect, performance result, or production fitness.
